instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F. Brush a rimmed baking sheet with the vegetable oil.
Rinse the betel leaves in cold water, then pat them dry with a clean towel. Lay them flat on a second towel with the shiny side down.
Mince the tender lower half of both lemongrass stalks. Finely chop 2 of the green onions, and slice the rest thinly for the end.

In a large bowl, combine the beef, the lemongrass, the 2 chopped green onions, 1 tsp fish sauce, the cornstarch, the five-spice, the sesame oil and the pepper. Mix with your hands for about 1 minute, until it looks sticky and you can't see any dry cornstarch.

Put about 2 tsp of the filling near the tip of a leaf, then roll it up to about 1/2 inch from the stem. Set it seam side down on the baking sheet. Repeat with the rest, leaving a little space between the rolls. That should be about 40 rolls.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the vermicelli.
Meanwhile, make the dipping sauce. Stir 5 tbsp fish sauce, 5 tbsp warm water and the sugar in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves. Mince the garlic and stir it in with the juice of the lime.

Bake the rolls for 5 minutes. Flip each one and bake for 3 minutes, until the leaves are dark and the filling feels firm. You're cooking the beef to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one roll there. No thermometer? Cut one open: it's done when there's no pink left.
While the rolls bake, cook the vermicelli for the time on the package, usually 3 to 5 minutes. Drain it and rinse it under cold water.
Tear the lettuce into pieces and pick the mint leaves.
Divide the vermicelli, lettuce and mint between 4 bowls and set the rolls on top. Scatter the sliced green onions over them and serve with the dipping sauce.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more sugar or a splash of fish sauce.
method_notes: Runaway Rice leads: a ground beef filling with lemongrass, green onion, fish sauce and five-spice, rolled in betel leaves and cooked at 450°F for 5 minutes, then flipped for 3. The other versions read (L'Academie, Helen's Recipes) add ground pork and peanuts and bake longer at 400°F; those were left out to keep this beef-only and nut-free. Oyster sauce was dropped (most brands contain wheat) and the dipping sauce is a plain nuoc cham in the proportions L'Academie gives. No version had 20 or more ratings. La lot is wild betel, not the chewing leaf; look for it fresh or frozen at Asian grocers.
